title: `log10` and `log(base)` divide natural logarithms
description: `log10()` is `log(10.0)`, and `log(base)` is Rust's `f64::log`, `ln(x) / ln(base)`: two roundings, so it can miss the correctly rounded result by an ulp. `log10(0.5)` is -0.30102999566398114 where `log10` gives -0.3010299956639812, and `log2(1e308)` is 1023.1538532253077 where `log2` gives 1023.1538532253076.

On `Float32` the same division runs in single precision, and the default base `math.e` becomes the float nearest e, whose `ln` rounds to 0.99999994. So the natural `log()` of a `Float32` misses by an ulp: `log(0.5)` is -0.69314724 where the correctly rounded value is -0.6931472, and `log10(0.5)` is -0.30102998 where it is -0.30103001. Recorded as PL-4.
The docs are silent on `log10` and `log` dividing two logarithms: a docs gap. The user guide promises no error bound.
No upstream test pins this; it may change between versions.
reference: `log10` and `log2` are the platform's `log10` and `log2`; only NULL, the sign and the domain are exact in the reference, the last bits are each engine's (#54).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: Equal float types: `x.log(base)` in that type; a float input casts the base to its type.
`f32::log` may not be correctly rounded; it is `ln(self) / ln(base)`.

notes: `log` keeps a `Float32` input in `Float32` (`log_dtype`) and computes `f32::log`, two single-precision roundings. The base literal is cast to `Float32`.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

provenance.notes: The correctly rounded `Float32` values of `ln(0.5)` and `log10(0.5)` are -0.693147182464599609375 and -0.30103000998497009277.

evidence.note: 'Compute the base 10 logarithm of the input array, element-wise'; no accuracy note. The body is `self.log(10.0)` (expr.py L914-L935).
Polars 'does not provide guarantees on the error unless mentioned otherwise' (SRC docs/source/user-guide/concepts/data-types-and-structures.md L186-L189).

`test_log`: [1, 3, 9, 27, 81].log(base [3, 3, 9, 3, 9]) == [0, 1, 1, 3, 2] for Float16/32/64 and mixed types, lazy collect() (both engines in CI), rel_tol 1e-5: pins result types and values, not the last bits.
`test_log_exp`: log10 of [1, 100, 1000] == [0, 2, 3], log vs np.log, rel_tol 1e-5. No upstream test pins the one-ulp misses of ln(x)/ln(base).
A float column with a base of another type casts the base to the column's type (math.e to 2.7182817 for Float32), then x.log(base) in f32.

provenance.notes: From the reverse pass's check of PL-4, which this fact records.
